author: cl-watch2
body:
[opus 5.5] Found and fixed. The race is in read_artifact_bytes (chat_runtime.rs), which every chat state document read goes through. It opens the record by path, then fstats what it opened and refuses it unless nlink == 1. Every record is written whole by atomic_json and renamed into place. A reader that does not hold the state lock can open the record just before a writer's rename lands. The file it opened then has no links left (nlink 0), so the reader refused it with "chat artifact is not a private owner-only regular file". deliver_request_with reads its request this way, as does queued_prompt on the way to submit. In the test, the acknowledgement worker spawned by spawn_ack_workers runs ensure_ack on the same request at the same moment. ensure_ack rewrites the request record twice under the state lock (Sending, then Acked). If the rename falls between the delivery pass's open and its fstat, deliver_request_with returns Err, process_keys_with_delivery records a 'deliver' error, and report.delivered is empty, which is the failure seen once at the census-audit gate on 2026-10-19. The window is between two syscalls, so only preemption under load opens it. That fits the 0-in-529 rate under #389 gate-flakes.

Reproduced deterministically: chat_runtime test a_record_replaced_while_a_lockless_read_opens_it_reads_as_its_earlier_copy runs the real ensure_ack between the reader's open and its fstat, through a new read_artifact_bytes_opened hook. With the old check it fails with exactly that error. nlink 0 on an opened file after a rename over it was also confirmed on this host's /tmp (btrfs).

Fix: an opened file with no links is read as the complete earlier copy it is, the one a read a moment sooner would have returned. The callers already tolerate a copy that goes stale right after it is read, and they re-read under the lock before they change anything. A record with more than one link (a hard link) is still refused, and the test checks that too. The assertions in the_acknowledgement_worker_adds_the_receipt_reaction_a_printed_prompt_earned are unchanged.

Unverified: the 2026-10-19 report was not captured, so nothing proves that failure took exactly this path rather than another error. It is the only path found that leaves delivered empty with no wait involved. If it recurs, the CycleReport printed by the assert says which: this race shows as errors [("deliver", <key>, "... not a private owner-only regular file ...")]. The Python edition keeps the strict check; its audit is #398 py-lockless-read-replaced.
